questions.q: How should a five-minute readout begin?
options: With a list of every report you built
With the headline answer to the manager's question
With the technical details of each formula
With an apology for missing data
questions.explain: Busy managers want the answer first. Findings, the recommendation, and caveats follow.

questions.q: An agent closes about 98 cases a month. Intake is 450 and closures are about 393. Roughly how much extra capacity is needed?
options: About 5 agents
About 2 agents
About 0.6 of an agent
No extra capacity
questions.explain: The shortfall is 450 - 393 = 57 cases a month, and 57 divided by 98 is about 0.6 of an agent.

questions.q: Why recommend process changes before headcount in this project?
options: Headcount can never be justified
Process changes cost nothing and always work
The data shows High-priority cases fail SLA most often and Low-priority volume may be reducible, so fix those before adding capacity
Managers dislike hiring
questions.explain: The analysis points to specific process issues. Capacity is justified if intake stays high after they are addressed.

questions.q: Which is a responsible choice for portfolio data?
options: Use a Developer Edition or sandbox with sample data you generated
Screenshot a real employer's live dashboards
Include customer names to make it realistic
Copy another analyst's portfolio
questions.explain: Portfolio work must never expose confidential employer or customer data. Sample-org data is safe.

questions.q: Why click through each dashboard tile to its source report before presenting?
options: To reconcile the tile with the report and catch mismatches before anyone else does
To make the dashboard refresh faster
To change the running user
Because dashboards cannot show numbers without it
questions.explain: Reconciliation protects your credibility. Any mismatch should be fixed before the readout.
